messages:
Ravi K.: quick thread — prototyping two alternate timeline behaviours for the Deployments history. one is a zoomable timeline (day/week/month) with an inset mini-map; the other is a continuous scroll with density heatmap. want feedback on discoverability + rollback UX.

Lin W.: mini-map feels promising for long histories. question: how do we surface canary windows vs full rollouts in a small map? color gradients or pattern overlays?

Maya G.: prefer a combination: color for state (canary=ramp=full) and a pattern (diagonal stripes) for active rollouts vs solid for completed. ensures color-only isn't the sole signal.

Eva R.: accessibility note: patterns + color is good. Also need text alternatives: the mini-map should have an aria-label like "timeline overview: 12 versions, 2 active rollouts" and focusable markers that read "version X, canary, 10%".

Ravi K.: agree. For the zoom controls, should we default to "week" or "month"? PM thinks week is more actionable; ops folks want month by default for long histories.

Lin W.: suggestion: default zoom = week for new orgs (few releases) and auto-switch to month when #versions > 50. Also save user preference.

Maya G.: microcopy for rollback button: current label "Revert" is terse and scares some product folks. Alternatives: "Rollback to this version" or "Start rollback". which is clearer?

Eva R.: "Start rollback" implies a process (good). But we need to be explicit about impact: tooltip + confirmation modal should say "This will route traffic back to this version. Some sessions may be interrupted." Also include an option to create a canary rollback (gradual) vs immediate.

Ravi K.: love the modal variant. For the modal CTA we should avoid destructive red for the main action if we offer a safe option. Maybe primary CTA = "Start gradual rollback" and a secondary red "Force rollback (all traffic)". That nudges safer defaults.

Lin W.: UX note: some users want quick keyboard rollback. If we gate force-rollbacks behind a secondary step, keyboard users shouldn't be blocked. maybe show keyboard shortcut in the modal and require typing the version number for force rollback (like github).

Maya G.: good point. Typing the version for destructive action is familiar. We'll add required confirm input for force rollback only.

Eva R.: heatmap option: when density mode is on, use tokenized tooltip content for each segment: percentage, error-rate, latency median. But be careful with live updates  if values change rapidly, we might spam screen readers. Use aria-live polite but debounce to 2s.

Ravi K.: deployment event: rollout 1987 -> ramp 50% at 2173456900 UTC (deploy-bot)

Lin W.: about the timeline rows: proposal to show an inline sparkline of latency/errors next to each version, small 24x48 px. On hover/focus show a larger chart. Keeps rows scannable but provides signal.

Maya G.: yes, but ensure sparklines are high-contrast and have an accessible description: "Latency sparkline: median 120ms, 95p 300ms". Also add alt text for compressed views.

Eva R.: keyboard focus order: when tabbing into a row, land on the expand control. pressing Enter expands. Next Tab goes to primary action (Start rollout / View diff). If force-action exists, it should be reachable via a secondary Tab and announced as destructive.

Ravi K.: one more: in the mini-map, clicking a marker should smoothly scroll the main timeline to that version and set focus on it. Smooth scroll needs a reduce-motion fallback.

Lin W.: for copy, avoid jargon in public dashboards. replace "canary" tooltip with "Canary (small-scale test)" and for internal-only orgs allow toggling advanced labels.

Maya G.: next steps: I'll mock both zoomable + continuous prototypes with the rollback modal flows. Eva, can you run a short SR test on both patterns? Lin, can you validate keyboard flows? Ravi will write the handoff ticket with copy variants.

Eva R.: I can test VoiceOver + NVDA tomorrow. I'll flag any issues in-thread.

Ravi K.: thanks all. I'll create the ticket and include acceptance criteria: 1) mini-map + zoom modes implemented, 2) rollback modal with gradual + force path, 3) sparklines with accessible labels, 4) keyboard order documented, 5) live-region debounced for rollout updates.

deploy-bot: noted event processed: rollout 1987 ramped to 50% at 2173456900 UTC

Maya G.: perfect. I'll attach mockups and copy options in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
